text: Shishak took Solomon's gold shields, and Rehoboam replaced them with bronze. Gold speaks of God's righteousness; bronze, of judgment.
explanation:
Because Rehoboam forsook the Lord, Shishak king of Egypt carried off the temple treasures, including all 300 gold shields Solomon had made. Rehoboam had bronze shields made in their place, and his guards carried them whenever he entered the temple. From a distance they shone just the same. It was all about appearances.

In Scripture, gold pictures divine righteousness and bronze pictures judgment, like the bronze altar where the sacrifice was judged. Paul says, "above all, taking the shield of faith"; in Greek, the faith: righteousness by faith. Much of the church has traded God's gift of righteousness for a righteousness of its own, with judgment built in. Don't settle for bronze that only looks like gold.

text: Saul fell with his shield "not anointed with oil." Soldiers oiled their shields the night before battle so arrows would glance off.
explanation:
A leather shield rubbed with oil grew taut and slick, so arrows slid off instead of sticking and burning. On Mount Gilboa, a high place that should have been Saul's advantage, "the shield of the mighty was cast away… the shield of Saul, not anointed with oil." The word means despised. The night before, Saul had been consulting a medium.

What was David doing that same season? His own men were talking of stoning him, but "David strengthened himself in the Lord his God," and he recovered everything. Keep your shield oiled: settled in His righteousness and full of His Spirit. Then the enemy's darts don't stick.

text: God never promised no weapon would be formed. He promised none would prosper.
explanation:
"No weapon formed against you shall prosper, and every tongue which rises against you in judgment you shall condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, and their righteousness is from Me." New viruses may mutate, symptoms may appear, critics may speak. Weapons will be formed.

But they're not there to stay. What the enemy forms against you will turn into a testimony of His glory. Notice whose promise this is: those whose righteousness is from Him. The more you declare, "I am the righteousness of God in Christ," the less you have to worry about the weapons or the critics.

text: The most powerful things of God work quietly: like your heartbeat, the sunset, the falling dew.
explanation:
You aren't supposed to hear your heart beating or your liver working; if you do, something's wrong. The sun sets without a sound. Dew settles while you sleep. Jesus came on a silent night, and Bethlehem never noticed. Then the devil reacted, loudly, with the slaughter of the infants.

The enemy works in the noisy realm of the senses: headlines, alarming numbers, frightening words. God initiates; the devil only plays catch-up. When the enemy attacks an area of your life, ask what God has just released there. "The things which are seen are temporary, but the things which are not seen are eternal."

text: When Jesus touched the leper, Jesus didn't catch leprosy. The leper caught what Jesus had.
explanation:
A leper was quarantined from everyone. He might not have felt a human hand in years. He only asked, "If You are willing, You can make me clean." He didn't ask to be touched, but "Jesus, moved with compassion, put out His hand and touched him."

Under the law, touching a leper made you unclean. With Jesus, it worked the other way: His life overpowered the disease. And He's in you. You can be infectious too, carrying His health, peace and healing into every place you go.

text: If Jesus took your guilt, don't take it back. Holding on to it puts you in a false position.
explanation:
Socrates once said, "It may be that the deity can forgive sins, but I do not see how." If God is righteous, He must punish evil; if He loves sinners, how can He accept them? The cross is the answer. "He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him." God isn't merely merciful in forgiving you; He's righteous in making you righteous.

So when you feel guilty and try to make up for it with good works, you're taking back what Jesus already carried. The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of truth; He can't bear witness to a lie. Before you pray, take your true place: "I am the righteousness of God in Christ." That's when heaven stops feeling like brass.

text: David ran toward Goliath. Fear shrinks when you walk toward it, and grows when you run away.
explanation:
"David hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine." He didn't cower behind a sling. Isaiah describes the opposite: "He who flees from the noise of fear shall fall into the pit, and he who comes up from the midst of the pit shall be caught in the snare." Running from fear only leads into the next trap.

Once, in a dream, a towering monster loomed overhead. But a holy anger rose up: "I will not respond to you." As the dreamer walked toward it, it grew smaller and more afraid, until it vanished. "The righteous are bold as a lion." That's you. Don't move at the voice of fear; move at the voice of the Spirit.
